messages.subject: [Basta-users] Question on survivorship for pre-emergence
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am busy sorting out my data to run with BaSTA. I have a question. In most
cases no data in available for pre-emergence litters. How does BaSTA
handles this? Or is it similar to ways previously used like in life-tables?

Thanks
Fabiano

messages.subject: [Basta-users] Question on survivorship for pre-emergence
messages.body_plain:
Hi Fabiano,
 
I guess you work on a species like the meerkat in which the young first
stay under the ground and you don't see them. You only see them for the
first time when they come above the ground and you have no idea how many
young died already before that. Is that right? In that case you could
use the argument minAge. You set it to the age when the young emerge and
BaSTA will then calculate survival from that age onwards.
 
Best wishes,
Maren

messages.subject: [Basta-users] Question on survivorship for pre-emergence
messages.body_plain:
Thanks. Let me see if I can re-formulate. The question is whether BaSTA
"assumes" that for example that cubs that are one month/year old have the
same survival probability as those that are a couple days old. The reason I
ask is that for certain species like the cheetahs a high mortality rate
prior the cubs leaving the "den", pre-emergence, is usually assumed.

My thinking is that it simply used the information based on observed cubs
to do so.

Hopefully, clearer.

Best,

2012/4/4 Colchero, Fernando <Colchero at demogr.mpg.de>
